pathway.title: Flutter Entertainment plc — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Flutter's total debt of USD 12,313 million at September 30, 2026 is almost unchanged from USD 12,266 million at December 31, 2025, but last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 2,331 million from USD 2,845 million, so total debt to Adjusted EBITDA rose to 5.28x from 4.31x and net debt to 4.55x from 3.67x [CP-1]. The reason is earnings, not borrowing: nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,499 million against USD 2,013 million, with the US segment down to USD 241 million from USD 612 million and the UK remote gaming duty rising from 21% to 40% in April 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The Group's own leverage ratio is 4.6x against 3.7x at December 31, 2025 and a 2.0x to 2.5x target, and management has paused share repurchases to prioritise deleveraging.

Liquidity is the main support. Flutter held USD 1,708 million of unrestricted cash and USD 782 million of undrawn revolver commitments at September 30, 2026, USD 2,490 million in all, or USD 2,477 million if the USD 13 million guarantee reservation is also deducted. No debt matures within twelve months beyond USD 52 million of scheduled repayments, and the October 30, 2026 amendment extends the term A loans and the revolver to May 3, 2032, so the 2028 repayment of USD 2,681 million largely moves out, leaving about USD 51 million of 2028 amortisation on an indicative basis. The next large maturity is USD 1,143 million in 2029, then USD 3,692 million in 2030. The sterling revolver headroom did shrink during 2026, from USD 1,185 million at March 31 to USD 782 million at September 30.

Interest is the pressure point. Cash interest paid was USD 636 million over the last twelve months, and the Group expects USD 696 million of interest in the next twelve months net of hedging, which is 3.35x covered by last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA (calculated). About USD 6,629 million of debt principal at December 31, 2025 was floating and unhedged, and the Group states that 100 basis points on rates added USD 61 million of annualised interest on its December 31, 2025 debt. Free cash flow after capital expenditure and interest was USD 515 million over the last twelve months, but only USD 319 million once player deposit movements are removed [CP-1]. That is thin against the cash costs now coming: an announced UK restructuring of USD 80 million to USD 90 million and potential legal settlements.

Claims outside debt are material but mostly uncrystallised. The Group discloses a Fast Code class action provision of USD 109 million awaiting judgment, an Indian GST demand of USD 527 million (provision USD 54 million), US tax notices proposing USD 181 million (no provision), Austrian claims of USD 52 million not accrued, and a Belgian claim of USD 27 million; the gross amounts without provision total USD 733 million (calculated), which is not an estimate of loss. Operating leases of USD 559 million and purchase commitments of USD 4,998 million sit outside debt. The Fox option over 18.6% of FanDuel is a contingent sale rather than a debt claim.

Debt ranking and market signals complete the picture. Every funded instrument, the term loans, the revolver and the five senior secured note series, is secured first priority on the same collateral and guaranteed by the same group of guarantors, so creditors share one pool and there is no junior or unsecured debt to absorb losses first. The senior secured notes had a quoted fair value of about 94% of carrying amount at September 30, 2026, against about 100% at December 31, 2025 (calculated), which shows the market has repriced the credit even though the Group reports compliance with all covenants. The leverage covenant moved from a net total leverage level of 5.20:1 to a net first lien leverage level of 5.70:1.00, but no covenant ratio value is printed, so the Group's own ratio of 4.6x cannot be read as headroom.

cells.text: Online sports betting and iGaming operator with sportsbook, iGaming and other products (exchange, pari-mutuel, daily fantasy sports, prediction markets).
Documentary Fact

These products are offered by FanDuel (sportsbook, iGaming and other products), Sky Betting & Gaming (sportsbook and iGaming products), Sportsbet (sportsbook products), PokerStars (iGaming products) (10-K page:8)
Many brands in many regulatory regimes spread licence and tax risk, but each market has its own cost of sales and tax rate.
The Group describes itself as the largest operator by revenue.
Management Language
Flutter is the world’s leading online sports betting and iGaming operator based on revenue. (10-K page:8)
Scale supports marketing efficiency and negotiating power; the claim is management's and not independently verified here.
Sportsbook is the largest product, iGaming second, and most revenue is online.
Documentary Fact

For fiscal 2025, 53% of our revenue was derived from sportsbook, 44% of our revenue was derived from iGaming, and 3% of our revenue was derived from other products, while 88% of our revenue at the Group level was generated from our online businesses. (10-K page:10)
Sportsbook revenue carries outcome variance; iGaming is steadier but more heavily taxed in some markets.
Sportsbook earns a spread on fixed odds; iGaming earns hold; poker and exchange earn rake or commission.
Documentary Fact
We generate revenue by setting odds in a manner that includes a theoretical spread to be earned on each contest less winnings paid and expenses associated with promotional activity. (10-K page:10)
Revenue is exposed to sports results in any period, so a run of customer-favourable results reduces earnings without changing volumes.
Two reportable segments: US and International.
Documentary Fact

The U.S. segment is our fastest growing and our largest region, constituting $6,967 million (or 43%) of our revenue for fiscal 2025. (10-K page:11); Our International segment constituted $9,416 million (or 57%) of our revenue for fiscal 2025. (10-K page:11)

International carries the larger share of earnings; the US is the growth and investment segment, so the two segments pull Adjusted EBITDA in different directions (CP-1: US 241 against 612 for nine months).
UKI, Southern Europe and Africa, Asia Pacific, CEE, Brazil and other regions.
Documentary Fact

Our UKI region constituted $3,547 million (or 22%) of our Group total revenue for fiscal 2025. (10-K page:12); Our Brazil region constituted $227 million (or 1%) of our Group total revenue for fiscal 2025. (10-K page:12)
The UK is the largest single international tax exposure; Brazil was small in revenue terms, so the ban's direct revenue loss is limited even though the impairment was large.
Management states leading shares in the states where FanDuel is live.
Management Language
we had an approximately 41% share of the online sports betting market in the states where FanDuel sportsbook was live (10-K page:11)
A leading share lowers customer acquisition risk in existing states but not the state tax risk.
Retail betting shops complement online.
Documentary Fact
Our online operations are complemented by 1,127 retail shops, mainly in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Italy and Serbia. (10-K page:10)
A small fixed-cost retail base; closures in the UKI restructuring would reduce fixed costs but not remove the UK tax.
US revenue follows major league calendars; one-off events affect volumes.
Documentary Fact
a majority of our current U.S. sports betting and DFS revenue is and will continue to be generated from bets placed on, or contests relating to, the NFL, the NBA, MLB and the NCAA (10-K page:12)
Quarterly cash flow is uneven, so liquidity should be tested at quarter ends, not only at year end.
UK remote gaming duty rises from 21% to 40% and betting duty from 15% to 25%; some US states raise rates.
Documentary Fact
an increase in remote gaming duty from 21% to 40% effective April 2026; and, an increase in betting duty (excluding horseracing and land-based) from 15% to 25% effective April 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:48)

Higher cost of sales in the UK reduces margin; the Group reports the UK duty as the main driver of the rise in International cost of sales (CP-1). A further rise in April 2027 is not yet in reported results.
Online betting and iGaming banned by executive order; Flutter stopped operating.
Documentary Fact
Flutter ceased operating sports betting and iGaming in Brazil on September 26, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:49)
Loss of the Brazilian revenue stream and a non-cash impairment (CP-1: 873); legal exposure remains (class action and NSX investigation, below).
Payments to US market access partners vary with revenue.
Documentary Fact

We make variable payments to the majority of our market access partners, typically based on a percentage of our revenue generated in the market where we use such market access partner’s skins. (10-K page:20)
Part of the US cost base flexes with revenue, which cushions a revenue fall but not a margin squeeze from tax.
Capital spending is mainly capitalized software and intangible purchases.
Analyst Interpretation
Capitalized software (397) (313) (Q3 10-Q page:9, nine months 2026 against 2025)
Product development is a recurring cash call that competes with debt service (CP-1: capital expenditure LTM 817).
Player deposits are held as cash and as a liability.
Documentary Fact
Player deposit liability 1,987 1,859 (Q3 10-Q page:6)
These balances are not available for debt service and move operating cash flow; liquidity should exclude them (CP-1 excludes them).
A new product line launched in partnership with CME.
Documentary Fact
In December 2025, we launched FanDuel Predicts in partnership with CME Group (“CME”) in five states. (Q3 10-Q page:46)
New product spend lowered US Adjusted EBITDA in Q3 2026 (release page:1); regulatory outcome is open (Supreme Court petition page:47).
The sources give player counts, not customer concentration measures.
Insufficient Information
Total Group AMPs 1 13,669 14,133 (Q3 10-Q page:50)
The consumer base is dispersed, but no concentration measure or retention data is disclosed beyond monthly players; this is not an adverse conclusion.

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification (Documentary Fact): Flutter operates two segments, the US at 43% and International at 57% of FY2025 revenue, with 88% of revenue online [CP-1A, company and operating model], which reduces dependence on any one market. Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation): USD 2,477 million of liquidity, USD 52 million of scheduled repayments within twelve months and an extension of term A and the revolver to May 2032 [CP-1, CP-1A transaction summary]. Cash generation (Documentary Fact): free cash flow remained positive at USD 515 million over the last twelve months after capital expenditure and cash interest [CP-1]. Deleveraging intent (Management Language): the Group has paused share repurchases and committed to returning to 2.0x to 2.5x over the medium term, which management states and has not yet achieved [CP-1A, governance table]. Structure (Documentary Fact): there is no sponsor, no dividend since May 2020 and no documented priming, uptiering or collateral release [CP-1A, company profile and governance table]; the sources cannot test legal capacity for any of these because the credit documents are not supplied.

Weaknesses. High and rising leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 5.28x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 4.55x against 4.31x and 3.67x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Earnings pressure (Documentary Fact): the UK gaming duty, the Brazil ban, which stopped operations on September 26, 2026 and produced a USD 873 million impairment, and weak US profit, partly from investment in prediction markets and new states [CP-1A, company and operating model]. Weakening cover (Documentary Fact): 3.67x on cash interest against 5.36x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation): Adjusted EBITDA excludes restructuring that is planned to run until 2029, legal loss contingencies of USD 200 million and share-based compensation, so cash costs fall below the reported line [CP-1 definition review]. Single collateral pool (Documentary Fact): all funded debt is first lien, so creditors depend on one claim on the same assets with no cushion below. Contingent claims (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information): the legal and tax matters above and the Fox option, whose rights on exercise are described as unresolved [CP-1A, credit translations]. Covenant opacity (Insufficient Information): headroom against the 5.20:1 and 5.70:1.00 tests is not calculable because covenant EBITDA and net borrowings definitions are not supplied.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In 2025 Flutter completed three acquisitions. On April 30, 2025 it bought 100% of Pluto (Italia) S.p.A, the holding company of Snai, for approximately $2.6 billion (€2.3 billion) (Q3 10-Q page:25). On May 14, 2025 it acquired a 56% interest in NSX for $674 million (BRL 3,799 million) with call and put options over the remainder (10-K page:9). It also acquired the 5% redeemable non-controlling interest in FanDuel held by Boyd for $1,553 million, taking its holding to 100% subject to the Fox option (10-K page:9). The accounting for Snai and NSX was finalised in the second quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:25, page:26). All three are documentary facts with status completed. The sources give acquisition terms only in these summaries, and no acquisition agreements are supplied.

The acquisitions were financed in stages. A €2.5 billion bridge term loan drawn on April 29, 2025 funded Snai, and a $1.75 billion bridge drawn on July 30, 2025 funded the Boyd transaction (10-K page:125, page:126). They were repaid with new $1,250 million of Term Loan B due June 4, 2032 ($750 million on June 4 and $500 million on August 7, 2025) and with the 2031 senior secured notes issued in the same two tranches: $1,625 million of 5.875%, €850 million of 4.000% and £700 million of 6.125% (10-K page:126, page:127, page:128). The 2029 notes of $525 million at 6.375% and €500 million at 5.000% had been issued by Flutter Treasury DAC on April 29, 2024 (10-K page:127). The use of proceeds was repayment of the bridges, general corporate purposes and costs (10-K page:126). Liquidity effect: the debt table shows total debt rising over 2025 (CP-1), and the Group states it believes it has sufficient capacity through cash, internal funds and the revolver (Q3 10-Q page:74, a management statement).

After the quarter, on October 30, 2026, the Group signed the First Amendment and Restatement Agreement to the November 2023 credit agreement (Q3 10-Q page:42). It extends the term A and revolver maturities to May 3, 2032, raises the revolver commitment to $1.86 billion with a US dollar base currency, redenominates term A into €382 million of term A2 loans and $1,374 million of term A3 loans, replaces the net total leverage covenant with a net first lien leverage covenant at 5.70:1.00, and prices term A and revolver loans at a margin of 1.40% to 2.00% set by corporate ratings (Q3 10-Q page:42). The revolver increase took effect on November 3, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:74). Status: completed, a subsequent event after September 30, 2026, described only in a note and in the Q3 release (page:12); the executed document is not supplied. The liquidity effect is an enlarged revolver, but the undrawn amount after the amendment is not disclosed. The Q3 release describes the facility increase as approximately $240m for the refinanced facilities without defining the set, which is not reconciled to the revolver figure (see conflicts).

Other transactions and structural changes: the Group delisted from the LSE on August 3, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:37); it paused the share repurchase programme during Q3 2026 (paused the 2024 Share Repurchase Program to prioritize deleveraging, Q3 10-Q page:75), having repurchased shares under the $5 billion authorisation (Q3 10-Q page:75); on October 20, 2026 it committed to a UKI restructuring plan affecting up to 1,400 employees with charges of $80 million to $90 million (Q3 10-Q page:42); and Brazil operations were closed in September and October 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:14). There is no sponsor, no dividend recapitalisation and no disposal described in the sources. No new debt issue is described after the October 30, 2026 amendment, and nothing is dated after the cutoff of November 5, 2026.

The 10-Q warns that `The definition of Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA Margin may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt agreements.` (`10-Q Q3 page:71`). Effect: the release ratio and the covenant ratio are not comparable, and the sources print no covenant ratio value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. **Covenant changes after quarter end.** The Q3 10-Q (`page:42`) says the amendment `replaces the net total leverage financial covenant with a net first lien leverage financial covenant and the financial covenant level increased to 5.70:1.00`. The 5.20:1 level in the 10-K applies to the pre-amendment test only. No source prints a first lien net leverage figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. **Facility size statements are not reconciled.** The Q3 release says the refinancing is `increasing the overall facility size by approximately $240m and extending the maturity date from November 2028 to May 2032` (`page:12`). The Q3 10-Q says the committed revolving facility `has been increased to $1.86 billion` (`page:75`), and the 10-K described `the Group’s $1.48 billion (£1.1 billion) committed revolving credit facility` (`page:125`). The release figure covers an undefined set of facilities; the sources do not show how it relates to the revolver figures. Effect: CP-2 must use the filing figures and treat the release figure as unreconciled.

fields.value: The CP-0 handoff was opened and used. It reports all four selected modules ready with limitations. This answer carries its limits forward: no executed credit documents, no covenant ratio values, the release leverage ratio and the covenant ratio use different definitions, and segment comparatives may not be recast. Where this answer settles a CP-0 question it says so under "Consistency with CP-0".

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The consolidated financial base is complete enough to use: audited FY2025 and FY2024 statements, three unaudited 2026 interim sets, a segment note, an Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation in every period and a debt note at each quarter end are all located. The picture they give is of a group whose total debt rose by 5,530 in 2025 (6,736 to 12,266, C13), with the proceeds of the 2025 term loan and note issues used to repay the bridge loans for the Snai acquisition and the Boyd transaction (10-K `page:126`), and whose earnings have since weakened. Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 is 1,499 against 2,013 for nine months 2025, driven by the US segment (241 against 612) and a higher UK gaming duty in International, while total debt is almost flat (12,313 at September 30, 2026 against 12,266 at December 31, 2025). Calculated total debt to Adjusted EBITDA therefore rises from 4.31x at FY2025 to 5.28x on a last-twelve-month basis, and the company's own net leverage ratio moves from 3.7x to 4.6x. Cash interest cover on the same basis falls from 5.36x to 3.67x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three features limit the view. First, the headline measure is the company's Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes share-based compensation, restructuring, legal loss contingencies, transaction costs and impairment; the 10-Q says its definition `may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt agreements`. Second, the last-twelve-month figures are calculated from annual and year-to-date data, and the segment comparatives for 2025 appear not to be recast for the 2026 customer transfers between regions. Third, cash flow from operations moves with player deposit balances, which are not the Group's own cash. The figures should be read as a documented reported base with calculated overlays, not as covenant tests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The three 2026 quarters sum to the nine-month figures printed in the Q3 10-Q (Adjusted EBITDA 1,499; net loss 1,235), and the three 2025 quarters sum to 2,013 and a net loss of 417 (C8). Q3 2026 net loss includes a Brazil impairment of 873 and a legal loss contingency add-back of 105 (Q3 10-Q `page:72` and `page:73`).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Adjusted EBITDA is defined in the Q3 10-Q as `income (loss) before income taxes; other (expense) income, net; interest expense, net; depreciation and amortization; transaction fees and associated costs; restructuring and integration costs; legal (settlements) loss contingencies; gaming tax disputes; impairment of property and equipment, intangible assets, right-of-use assets and goodwill; and share-based compensation charge` (`page:70`). The 10-K notes that `Beginning January 1, 2024, the Group revised its definition of Adjusted EBITDA` (`page:99`); FY2024 and FY2023 figures in the 10-K are on the revised basis, and no earlier basis is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Items excluded in the nine months to September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:72`): share-based compensation 176, transaction fees 32, restructuring and integration costs 254, legal loss contingencies 200 and impairment 873. The restructuring programmes `are expected to run until 2029` (`page:73`), so the restructuring add-back is recurring in practice. Cash cost of the UKI restructuring, `$80 million to $90 million` pre-tax, is announced after quarter end (`page:42`) and is not in any period shown.

fields.value: - Operating lease cost is inside Adjusted EBITDA (it is an operating expense), and operating lease liabilities sit outside debt. No finance lease balance is printed; the 10-K says `Substantially all leases are long-term operating leases` (`page:186`).

Its net debt adds back unamortized costs and removes unrealized foreign exchange on hedged debt (Q3 release `page:26`). This answer uses carrying total debt less unrestricted cash, so its net debt (10,605) is lower than the release's (10,656) by 51. fields.value: - **Leverage.** Evidence: total debt 12,313 at September 30, 2026 against 12,266 at December 31, 2025 (`Total debt 12,313 12,266`, Q3 10-Q `page:26`), while LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 2,331 against 2,845. Mechanism: the 2025 acquisition debt is in place for the full period, and earnings fell in the US segment (241 against 612 for nine months) and from the UK gaming duty in International (Q3 10-Q `page:70`: `an increase of remote gaming tax in UK`). Consequence: calculated total leverage rose by about one turn between FY2025 and Q3 2026, and the company itself targets `2.0 - 2.5x` (Q3 release `page:12`).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - **Cover.** Evidence: cash interest paid 636 over the last twelve months against 531 in FY2025. Mechanism: a full year of interest on the notes due 2031 and Term Loan B due 2032 issued in 2025 (Q3 10-Q `page:53`: `a full quarter of interest on the Senior Secured Notes due 2031 and the USD First Lien Term Loan B due 2032 issued in August 2025`). Consequence: cover on cash interest fell from 5.36x to 3.67x, and the next twelve months carry `$696 million payable within 12 months net of hedging` of scheduled interest (Q3 10-Q `page:74`).

fields.value: - **Cash flow.** Evidence: free cash flow of 377 for 9M 2026 against 269 for 9M 2025, but 201 against 396 once player deposit movements are removed. Mechanism: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was lifted by player funds (176) and higher accrued legal and gaming duty liabilities (Q3 10-Q `page:76`). Consequence: the improvement in reported free cash flow is not evidence of stronger underlying cash generation; share repurchases of 543 over the last twelve months exceeded free cash flow of 515, and the programme is now paused (Q3 10-Q `page:75`).

Mechanism: the revolver was drawn to fund operations and repayments (`drew £1,208 million ($1,621 million)`, Q3 10-Q `page:27`). Consequence: the sterling revolver headroom fell from 1,185 at March 31, 2026 to 782; the post-amendment commitment is larger, but its undrawn amount is not supplied.

Mechanism: impairment of 873 on Brazil, legal loss contingencies of 200 and restructuring of 254 are excluded. Consequence: cash costs among those items (legal settlements, restructuring severance) will reduce free cash flow in later periods even though they do not reduce Adjusted EBITDA.

fields.value: Flutter is an Ireland-incorporated, New York-headquartered online sports betting and iGaming group whose shares trade on the NYSE, with no sponsor and no controlling shareholder identified in the pack. Its revenue base is large and diversified by geography and product, with about 88% of FY2025 revenue earned online and the rest mainly through retail shops in the UK, Ireland, Italy and Serbia. Sportsbook revenue depends on the margin Flutter earns on fixed-odds bets, so it moves with sports results and with the sporting calendar; iGaming revenue is less dependent on the calendar. Both are exposed to gaming taxes that governments change at short notice, and the last year shows how fast this transmits: the UK raised remote gaming duty sharply in April 2026, Brazil's executive ban closed Flutter's Brazilian operations within days in September 2026, and India's 2025 ban ended Junglee. In India and Brazil Flutter took impairments, and in the UK it announced a restructuring.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction history matters more to a creditor than the operating model. In 2025 the Group bought Snai in Italy, a 56% stake in NSX in Brazil, and the 5% of FanDuel held by Boyd, funding them with bridge loans refinanced by new term loan B and senior secured notes issued in June and August 2025. Total debt rose as a result (CP-1), while Brazil, bought with NSX in May 2025, was shut down within sixteen months and carries a large impairment. Management has since paused share repurchases to prioritise deleveraging and set a target leverage range, but earnings fell in 2026 and leverage is well above that range (CP-1). The contingent claim of Fox on FanDuel, a new CEO from October 1, 2026, a UKI restructuring and a credit agreement amendment on October 30, 2026 are subsequent changes that the debt and covenant modules must treat as post-period events. The amendment is known only from filing summaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2025 Flutter completed three acquisitions. On April 30, 2025 it bought 100% of Pluto (Italia) S.p.A, the holding company of Snai, for approximately `$2.6 billion (€2.3 billion)` (Q3 10-Q `page:25`). On May 14, 2025 it acquired a 56% interest in NSX for `$674 million (BRL 3,799 million)` with call and put options over the remainder (10-K `page:9`). It also acquired the 5% redeemable non-controlling interest in FanDuel held by Boyd for `$1,553 million`, taking its holding to 100% subject to the Fox option (10-K `page:9`). The accounting for Snai and NSX was finalised in the second quarter of 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:25`, `page:26`). All three are documentary facts with status completed. The sources give acquisition terms only in these summaries, and no acquisition agreements are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisitions were financed in stages. A `€2.5 billion` bridge term loan drawn on April 29, 2025 funded Snai, and a `$1.75 billion` bridge drawn on July 30, 2025 funded the Boyd transaction (10-K `page:125`, `page:126`). They were repaid with new `$1,250 million` of Term Loan B due June 4, 2032 (`$750 million` on June 4 and `$500 million` on August 7, 2025) and with the 2031 senior secured notes issued in the same two tranches: `$1,625 million of 5.875%`, `€850 million of 4.000%` and `£700 million of 6.125%` (10-K `page:126`, `page:127`, `page:128`). The 2029 notes of `$525 million` at 6.375% and `€500 million` at 5.000% had been issued by Flutter Treasury DAC on April 29, 2024 (10-K `page:127`). The use of proceeds was repayment of the bridges, general corporate purposes and costs (10-K `page:126`). Liquidity effect: the debt table shows total debt rising over 2025 (CP-1), and the Group states it believes it has sufficient capacity through cash, internal funds and the revolver (Q3 10-Q `page:74`, a management statement).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the quarter, on October 30, 2026, the Group signed the First Amendment and Restatement Agreement to the November 2023 credit agreement (Q3 10-Q `page:42`). It extends the term A and revolver maturities to `May 3, 2032`, raises the revolver commitment to `$1.86 billion` with a US dollar base currency, redenominates term A into `€382 million of term A2 loans and $1,374 million of term A3 loans`, replaces the net total leverage covenant with a net first lien leverage covenant at `5.70:1.00`, and prices term A and revolver loans at a margin of `1.40% to 2.00%` set by corporate ratings (Q3 10-Q `page:42`). The revolver increase took effect on November 3, 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:74`). Status: completed, a subsequent event after September 30, 2026, described only in a note and in the Q3 release (`page:12`); the executed document is not supplied. The liquidity effect is an enlarged revolver, but the undrawn amount after the amendment is not disclosed. The Q3 release describes the facility increase as approximately `$240m` for the refinanced facilities without defining the set, which is not reconciled to the revolver figure (see conflicts).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions and structural changes: the Group delisted from the LSE on August 3, 2026 (Q2 10-Q `page:37`); it paused the share repurchase programme during Q3 2026 (`paused the 2024 Share Repurchase Program to prioritize deleveraging`, Q3 10-Q `page:75`), having repurchased shares under the `$5 billion` authorisation (Q3 10-Q `page:75`); on October 20, 2026 it committed to a UKI restructuring plan affecting up to `1,400 employees` with charges of `$80 million to $90 million` (Q3 10-Q `page:42`); and Brazil operations were closed in September and October 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:14`). There is no sponsor, no dividend recapitalisation and no disposal described in the sources. No new debt issue is described after the October 30, 2026 amendment, and nothing is dated after the cutoff of November 5, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legal capacity (what the documents permit) is not assessable from the pack; willingness is shown by the documented repurchase pause and acquisition funding; feasibility is addressed by CP-1 (leverage and liquidity at Q3 2026) and CP-2.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. **Revenue durability.** Evidence: the revenue mix and regional split above (10-K `page:10`, `page:11`, `page:12`). Risk mechanic: revenue is spread over two segments, about 100 countries and many brands, so no single market is decisive; but sportsbook margin moves with sports results and tax rates are set by governments. Credit implication: diversification reduces the chance that one regulatory event impairs debt service, while regular tax and regulatory shocks reduce visibility of EBITDA and leave less room for leverage. Counter-evidence: the Brazil ban removed a region that was only 1% of FY2025 revenue, so geographic spread has so far limited revenue loss from individual bans.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. **Margin and cash flow risk.** Evidence: UK remote gaming duty from 21% to 40% (Q3 10-Q `page:48`) and the UKI restructuring of up to 1,400 jobs with charges of `$80 million to $90 million` (Q3 10-Q `page:42`). Risk mechanic: the duty is charged within cost of sales, which lowered International margin in 2026 (CP-1); mitigation costs are cash and excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. Credit implication: cash conversion falls before savings arrive, which weighs on interest cover in the next twelve months (CP-1: LTM cover on cash interest of 3.67x), and a further duty rise is scheduled for April 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. **Concentration risk.** Evidence: US 43% of FY2025 revenue and the seasonality statement (10-K `page:11`, `page:12`). Risk mechanic: US earnings depend on league calendars, state tax changes (`North Carolina, where the sports betting tax rate increased from 18% to 23%`, Q3 10-Q `page:48`) and prediction market investment. Credit implication: the segment that the Group calls its largest growth opportunity (`We believe that our U.S. segment is the largest growth opportunity for the Group.`, Q3 10-Q `page:47`) currently produces the weakest earnings (CP-1: US Adjusted EBITDA of 241 for nine months 2026), so debt service relies on International for now. No customer concentration is disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. **Ownership, sponsor alignment and the Fox option.** Evidence: no sponsor, no controlling holder identified; a Fox call option over 18.6% of FanDuel units at `$4.8 billion` as of December 31, 2025, compounding 5% a year, exercisable until December 2030 (10-K `page:29`, `page:132`). Risk mechanic: exercise requires cash payment to the Group, which would bring cash but reduce the Group's economic interest in FanDuel and could give Fox consent rights over matters such as acquisitions and debt incurrence if the former Fastball rights carry over; the filing says it `has not been determined what specific rights Fox may receive`. Credit implication: a possible deleveraging event with a loss of control over the largest growth asset; the timing is at Fox's choice and Fox must be licensed to exercise (10-K `page:132`). Fair value of the liability fell from 560 at December 31, 2025 to 100 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q `page:33`), a change that reflects management's valuation assumptions; the sources do not explain it in the pages read here. Counter-evidence: none logged.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. **Capital allocation and leverage tolerance.** Evidence: debt-funded acquisitions, repurchases under the `$5 billion` programme, and the pause (Q3 10-Q `page:75`; Q3 release `page:1`). Risk mechanic: leverage at Q3 2026 is well above the stated range (CP-1), repurchases continued in the first half of 2026 before the pause (Q3 10-Q `page:7`, share repurchases in the first and second quarters), and the amendment raised the covenant level (`5.70:1.00`). Credit implication: leverage tolerance is high and the deleveraging path depends on earnings recovery and cash generation, which management has guided but not delivered (CP-1: net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 4.55x against the 2.0 to 2.5x target).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. **Key uncertainties.** Legal and tax matters with amounts disclosed (Indian GST demand of `₹50.6 billion ($527 million)` against a recorded `$54 million`, IRS proposed adjustments of about `$181 million` with no provision, and the Brazilian class action and NSX investigation; Q3 10-Q `page:41`, `page:49`, `page:50`) and the unavailability of the executed credit documents. Credit implication: these are claims outside the debt figure that could use cash or restrict financing; their size cannot be tied to covenant definitions from this pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: None. This module makes no calculation. Every figure is quoted from a cited source page or referenced from the accepted CP-1 handoff (LTM Adjusted EBITDA 2,331, total debt 12,313, cash 1,708, total debt to Adjusted EBITDA 5.28x, net debt to Adjusted EBITDA 4.55x, LTM cash interest cover 3.67x, nine-month US Adjusted EBITDA 241, capital expenditure LTM 817, impairment 873).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CP-2 runs next on the debt structure and should take from this answer: the transaction history behind the debt (the 2025 acquisition financing and the 2029 and 2031 notes), the October 30, 2026 amendment as a subsequent event described only in filing summaries, the unreconciled facility-size statements, the Fox option and minority put and call rights as claims outside debt, the open legal and tax matters, and the absence of any documented creditor-adverse action together with the absence of the documents needed to assess legal capacity. CP-5 should verify the locators and quotes in this answer, and in particular the conflicts table and the credit translations that cite CP-1 references. The next evidence action is to obtain the credit agreement amendment, the indenture and the covenant definitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is the fundamental credit synthesis for Flutter Entertainment plc (issuer id `flut`), as of 2026-11-05, on the `credit_snapshot` pathway. It covers the consolidated group's debt structure, liquidity, covenants, claims outside debt and events through the November 5, 2026 cutoff, in US dollars, for Q3 2026 against FY2025. It builds on the accepted source readiness, financial base and business handoffs and on the seven pinned filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All three handoffs were opened and used. Locators are `page:N` of the pinned `.jsonl` text. Figures marked "calculated" are derived in `## Calculations`.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Flutter's debt is adequately supported but stretched: the group is large, diversified and still cash generative, yet total debt to Adjusted EBITDA has risen to 5.28x and net debt to 4.55x, well above management's 2.0x to 2.5x target. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,477 million at September 30, 2026 and no sizeable maturity before 2029 once the October 2026 amendment is counted. The weakest point is earnings: higher UK gaming duty, the Brazil ban and weak US profit cut last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA to USD 2,331 million. What decides the outcome is whether cost actions and the buyback pause bring leverage down before further tax rises and legal settlements, and the covenant headroom for that cannot be measured from these sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Flutter's total debt of USD 12,313 million at September 30, 2026 is almost unchanged from USD 12,266 million at December 31, 2025, but last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 2,331 million from USD 2,845 million, so total debt to Adjusted EBITDA rose to 5.28x from 4.31x and net debt to 4.55x from 3.67x [CP-1]. The reason is earnings, not borrowing: nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was USD 1,499 million against USD 2,013 million, with the US segment down to USD 241 million from USD 612 million and the UK remote gaming duty rising from 21% to 40% in April 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The Group's own leverage ratio is 4.6x against 3.7x at December 31, 2025 and a 2.0x to 2.5x target, and management has paused share repurchases to prioritise deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the main support. Flutter held USD 1,708 million of unrestricted cash and USD 782 million of undrawn revolver commitments at September 30, 2026, USD 2,490 million in all, or USD 2,477 million if the USD 13 million guarantee reservation is also deducted. No debt matures within twelve months beyond USD 52 million of scheduled repayments, and the October 30, 2026 amendment extends the term A loans and the revolver to May 3, 2032, so the 2028 repayment of USD 2,681 million largely moves out, leaving about USD 51 million of 2028 amortisation on an indicative basis. The next large maturity is USD 1,143 million in 2029, then USD 3,692 million in 2030. The sterling revolver headroom did shrink during 2026, from USD 1,185 million at March 31 to USD 782 million at September 30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest is the pressure point. Cash interest paid was USD 636 million over the last twelve months, and the Group expects USD 696 million of interest in the next twelve months net of hedging, which is 3.35x covered by last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA (calculated). About USD 6,629 million of debt principal at December 31, 2025 was floating and unhedged, and the Group states that 100 basis points on rates added USD 61 million of annualised interest on its December 31, 2025 debt. Free cash flow after capital expenditure and interest was USD 515 million over the last twelve months, but only USD 319 million once player deposit movements are removed [CP-1]. That is thin against the cash costs now coming: an announced UK restructuring of USD 80 million to USD 90 million and potential legal settlements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside debt are material but mostly uncrystallised. The Group discloses a Fast Code class action provision of USD 109 million awaiting judgment, an Indian GST demand of USD 527 million (provision USD 54 million), US tax notices proposing USD 181 million (no provision), Austrian claims of USD 52 million not accrued, and a Belgian claim of USD 27 million; the gross amounts without provision total USD 733 million (calculated), which is not an estimate of loss. Operating leases of USD 559 million and purchase commitments of USD 4,998 million sit outside debt. The Fox option over 18.6% of FanDuel is a contingent sale rather than a debt claim.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt ranking and market signals complete the picture. Every funded instrument, the term loans, the revolver and the five senior secured note series, is secured first priority on the same collateral and guaranteed by the same group of guarantors, so creditors share one pool and there is no junior or unsecured debt to absorb losses first. The senior secured notes had a quoted fair value of about 94% of carrying amount at September 30, 2026, against about 100% at December 31, 2025 (calculated), which shows the market has repriced the credit even though the Group reports compliance with all covenants. The leverage covenant moved from a net total leverage level of 5.20:1 to a net first lien leverage level of 5.70:1.00, but no covenant ratio value is printed, so the Group's own ratio of 4.6x cannot be read as headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and diversification (Documentary Fact): Flutter operates two segments, the US at 43% and International at 57% of FY2025 revenue, with 88% of revenue online [CP-1A, company and operating model], which reduces dependence on any one market. Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation): USD 2,477 million of liquidity, USD 52 million of scheduled repayments within twelve months and an extension of term A and the revolver to May 2032 [CP-1, CP-1A transaction summary]. Cash generation (Documentary Fact): free cash flow remained positive at USD 515 million over the last twelve months after capital expenditure and cash interest [CP-1]. Deleveraging intent (Management Language): the Group has paused share repurchases and committed to returning to 2.0x to 2.5x over the medium term, which management states and has not yet achieved [CP-1A, governance table]. Structure (Documentary Fact): there is no sponsor, no dividend since May 2020 and no documented priming, uptiering or collateral release [CP-1A, company profile and governance table]; the sources cannot test legal capacity for any of these because the credit documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. High and rising leverage (Documentary Fact): total debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 5.28x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 4.55x against 4.31x and 3.67x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Earnings pressure (Documentary Fact): the UK gaming duty, the Brazil ban, which stopped operations on September 26, 2026 and produced a USD 873 million impairment, and weak US profit, partly from investment in prediction markets and new states [CP-1A, company and operating model]. Weakening cover (Documentary Fact): 3.67x on cash interest against 5.36x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation): Adjusted EBITDA excludes restructuring that is planned to run until 2029, legal loss contingencies of USD 200 million and share-based compensation, so cash costs fall below the reported line [CP-1 definition review]. Single collateral pool (Documentary Fact): all funded debt is first lien, so creditors depend on one claim on the same assets with no cushion below. Contingent claims (Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information): the legal and tax matters above and the Fox option, whose rights on exercise are described as unresolved [CP-1A, credit translations]. Covenant opacity (Insufficient Information): headroom against the 5.20:1 and 5.70:1.00 tests is not calculable because covenant EBITDA and net borrowings definitions are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Notes on the table. The credit agreement is `Term Loan A, Term Loan B and Revolving Credit Facility Agreement` dated November 24, 2023 with J.P. Morgan SE as administrative agent (10-K `page:125`). The notes may be redeemed at prices set in the indenture from April 15, 2026 (2029 notes) and from April 15, 2027 (2031 notes) (10-K `page:129`); make-whole and equity-claw terms applied before those dates. Until April 15, 2027 the Issuer may redeem up to 40% of each 2031 series with equity proceeds at 105.875% (USD), 104% (EUR) and 106.125% (GBP) of principal (10-K `page:129`). The Group states the notes `rank pari passu in right of payment with all existing and future senior debt of the Issuer that is not subordinated to the Notes` (10-K `page:128`). After the October 30, 2026 amendment, term A2 loans of `€382 million` and term A3 loans of `$1,374 million` are outstanding, no sterling term A loans remain, and the revolver commitment is `$1.86 billion` in US dollars (10-Q Q3 `page:42`). Term A and revolver loans then bear Term SOFR, EURIBOR or SONIA plus `1.40% to 2.00%` depending on the corporate ratings of Moody's, S&P and Fitch (10-Q Q3 `page:42`); no rating is stated in any source. Hedges: interest rate swaps with a notional of USD 1,489 million convert part of Term Loan B to fixed until June 30, 2027; a cross-currency swap of USD 525 million converts the 2029 USD notes to sterling until April 18, 2028; and fair value hedges of USD 500 million and USD 1,000 million relate to the 2031 USD notes until June 4, 2027 (10-Q Q3 `page:28`, `page:29`).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The revolver availability history in the three 2026 quarters is `$1,185 million (£895 million)` at March 31, `$1,081 million (£815 million)` at June 30 and `$782 million (£590 million)` at September 30 (10-Q Q1 `page:20`, 10-Q Q2 `page:23`, 10-Q Q3 `page:27`). The Group drew `£1,208 million ($1,621 million)` and repaid `£1,108 million ($1,492 million)` under the revolver in the nine months (10-Q Q3 `page:27`).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other covenants: the agreement limits additional debt, liens, distributions, restricted payments, acquisitions, disposals and amendments of other debt, `in each case subject to certain permitted exceptions` (10-K `page:128`); the baskets are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third quarter of 2026 brought a Brazilian impairment of USD 873 million, a provision for the Fast Code class action, quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of USD 360 million against USD 478 million, a pause in share repurchases, and a cut to 2026 guidance to Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2.495 billion at the midpoint, down USD 160 million [CP-1, Q3 release]. After September 30, 2026 the Group committed to the UKI restructuring on October 20, 2026, signed the credit agreement amendment on October 30, 2026 (revolver increase effective November 3, 2026) and published results on November 4, 2026 [CP-1A timeline]. Nothing dated after the November 5, 2026 cutoff is used. The next UK tax step, betting duty from 15% to 25% in April 2027, is announced but not yet in any reported period.

fields.value: - This answer corrects a reading in the financial base handoff. That handoff described the undrawn revolver figures as including the USD 13 million guarantee reservation. The sterling arithmetic points the other way: the commitment of £1.10 billion less drawings of £500 million less the £10 million reservation equals the printed £590 million, and the same holds at the other three dates (C2). The reservation therefore appears already deducted, so liquidity is USD 2,490 million on that reading and USD 2,477 million on the conservative one. This answer uses USD 2,477 million.

This is a reading, not a statement in the sources, so the item stays logged as unconfirmed.
